brief.analysis: This is the clearest broken band: raw_and_detrended_diverge is true (raw z 1.65 vs detrended 0.59), direct evidence the ratio's mean is trending up rather than sitting flat, and that fits a structural multi-year rearmament regime with NATO defense spending at record highs. The 200DMA is already achieved, the 50DMA slope is not confirmed, and the base rate is a coin-flip 3/6 — so the 5-year mean (+17.6% further) is an invalid, backward-looking target and the statistics are a trap here.
brief.report_line: Avoid shorting ITA/SPY toward its 5-year mean — record, multi-year NATO defense spending has structurally re-rated the ratio, the mean is drifting up, and the reversion target is stale.

brief.analysis: SMH is the purest AI-capex vehicle inside QQQ, so semis structurally taking index share is the live regime story rather than a pure dislocation — and with ma_score 0/3 and the 50DMA slope still intact, the ratio hasn't even begun to roll over. But raw and detrended z agree (3.17 vs 3.21), meaning the stretch is real even against the ratio's own uptrend, and the 6/8 forward base rate is genuine; I trust the 200DMA target (+22%) far more than the 5y mean (+78%), which is a fantasy in an AI-capex regime.
brief.report_line: Short SMH/QQQ against the 200DMA only — the trend is intact and the 5-year mean is stale in an AI-capex regime, so this is a size-down, wait-for-the-roll-over trade, not a full-conviction reversion.
